extracted.intended_audience: authors, referees and editors submitting to or working with EMBO Press journals (life sciences researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and publication standards and criteria used by EMBO Press/EMBO Journal to evaluate, process and present life-science research papers, emphasizing transparency, data integrity, presentation, and editorial timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent Process (publication of referee reports and editorial communication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key attributes include the publication of referee reports and editorial communication alongside papers — a feature almost all authors choose now — detailed editorial decisions, the exclusion of confidential referee remarks and, most importantly, the focus on only essential experimental revision with clear communication of the requirements for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish referee reports and editorial correspondence with the paper; exclude confidential referee remarks; clearly communicate which experimental revisions are essential. The policy has been developed over ~5 years and is applied across EMBO Press journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing after one revision / focus on essential experimental revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on only essential experimental revision with clear communication of the requirements for publication; aim to publish after a single round of experimental revision wherever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical performance: 95–97% acceptance of invited revisions, 90–92% accepted after a single round of experimental revision (average revision time 74 days). Editorial decisions are made within 1 week and peer review is completed in 1 month. Revisions should be constructive and proportionate to the importance of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee interaction and author response before decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Invite referees to comment on each other's reports and, where warranted, invite an author response to referee comments before the editorial decision is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice helps ensure balanced decisions and can dramatically improve a manuscript. It may be used in the three years since its adoption to ensure fairness and balance in recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind peer review option
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer a double-blind peer review option for authors who have concerns that author name or affiliation may influence referee opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This option will be available in response to community requests and is applied across EMBO Press publications to mitigate bias based on identity or affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial assessment ignores intervening publications during revision
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial assessment does not take into account other papers published during peer review or revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages authors to take the time necessary for constructive revision without penalty for relevant new work published elsewhere while the manuscript is under review/being revised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepublication data integrity checks (systematic figure checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically check all figures in manuscripts that are poised to be accepted for publication to identify image and data processing problems or other ethical concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings: issues in >20% of manuscripts reviewed at this stage; most are 'data beautification' and are resolved in revision, but some are unresolvable and would have required correction of the published record. These checks are standardized across EMBO journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics expert advisors and author checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt author checklists and appoint ethics expert advisors to the editorial advisory boards to standardize processes related to data integrity and ethical concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use checklists and ethics expertise to catch and resolve problems before publication. These measures form part of EMBO Press standardization across journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace Supplementary Information with Expanded View figures
rubrics_metrics.description: All data and information essential to support the author's conclusions is contained in peer-reviewed and copy-edited figures in the paper; supplementary data are replaced by 'Expanded View' figures presented in the main manuscript (collapsible) rather than hidden supplementary files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanded View can include controls, replicates, negative results, extended methods/protocols, algorithms, code, models and datasets. Tangential or peripheral data should not form part of an EMBO Press paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude tangential or peripheral data from the main paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Tangential or peripheral data should no longer form part of an EMBO Press paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only data essential to support conclusions should be in the peer-reviewed paper; peripheral information may appear in less detailed (collapsible) Expanded View but should not clutter the main narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Source Data underlying key findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage the presentation of Source Data underlying the figures representing key findings in the paper (e.g., uncropped micrographs/blots and data files used to generate graphs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More than one-third of papers included such data in the referenced year. Source Data make results more informative and reproducible; authors are encouraged to provide structured source files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer presentation of source measurements over unnecessary statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Press encourages inclusion of statistics only where appropriate and instead to present source data for the individual measurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where feasible, provide raw/individual measurements to enable readers to assess variability and reproducibility; use summary statistics judiciously rather than as a substitute for underlying data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated scientific data editors to optimize presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Dedicated scientific data editors work with the authors on the optimized and structured presentation of their figures and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data editors help avoid making publishing more cumbersome by assisting with presentation, structuring of Source Data, and preparing Expanded View figures so that papers become enriched, accessible records of research data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layered paper structure and enhanced accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: View the paper as a layered structure that allows the reader access to their preferred level of detail, from title/abstract/synopsis down to the actual data; main paper optimized for the general reader while deeper levels provide source data, structured datasets or code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short synopses and visual abstracts (designed with authors) to make papers more accessible; develop data-oriented search technology to improve discoverability and reach a broad readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for research that is well-supported, reproducible and conceptually advanced
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers should be able to rely on research that is well-supported and reproducible, and papers should provide a high level of conceptual advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial processes, data checks, Source Data, and peer review practices are designed to ensure robustness and conceptual novelty; authors should provide sufficient evidence and clarity to demonstrate conceptual contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency, accountability and best-practice across EMBO publications
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Press stands for innovation, reliability, fairness and best practice; deliver enhanced functionality, content and design and a consistent set of constructive policies, editorial processes and quality standards across the four EMBO publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same transparent processes (reports, checks, Expanded View, data editors etc.) across journals to add maximal value and to hold journals accountable to authors and readers.
